body:
### Problem

`getdecchrs()` in `src/nvim/regexp.c` reads a decimal number into an `int64_t` with no upper
bound:

```c
static int64_t getdecchrs(void)
{
  int64_t nr = 0;
  ...
    nr *= 10;          // regexp.c:1131, overflows for 20+ digits
    nr += c - '0';
```

A number with 20 or more digits overflows `int64_t`, which is undefined behavior. In practice
the value wraps around, and the range checks in the callers see the wrapped value:

- `\%d99999999999` is rejected with `E678: Invalid character after \%[dxouU]` (correct),
- `\%d18446744073709551713` (= 2^64 + 97) wraps to 97 and silently matches `a` (wrong).

Both regexp engines are affected. The same helper is used for `[\d123]` inside a collection
and for the lookbehind limit `\@123<=`, so those wrap the same way.
(`\%23l`, `\%23c` and `\%23v` use a separate loop and are not affected.)

This is the same code as in Vim, reported there as vim/vim#21668. In Vim `nr` is unsigned, so
there it is "only" a wrong match; in Nvim it is also signed overflow. An earlier Vim report,
vim/vim#2254, was closed after patch 8.0.1254, which widened the type from `int` to `long` but
added no bound, so the overflow moved from 10 to 20 digits. If Vim fixes #21668, porting that
patch would fix this too.

A possible fix is to stop growing the number once it is out of range, while still consuming
all digits as the function comment says:

```c
    if (nr <= INT_MAX) {  // larger values are invalid anyway, avoid overflow
      nr = nr * 10 + (c - '0');
    }
```

With that, `\%d<huge>` gives E678 like `\%d99999999999` does today, and `[\d<huge>]` is
clamped to `INT_MAX` by `coll_get_char()` like other large values.

Found by fuzzing the regexp engines with libFuzzer + UBSan

### Steps to reproduce


`match('xab', pat)` returns the index of the first match of `pat` in `"xab"` (`x`=0, `a`=1,
`b`=2). `\%d97` matches the character with decimal code 97, `a`.

```sh
nvim --clean --headless +"echo match('xab', '\%d97')" +q
# 1                                          (ok: 'a')
nvim --clean --headless +"echo match('xab', '\%d99999999999')" +q
# E678: Invalid character after \%[dxouU]    (ok: rejected)
nvim --clean --headless +"echo match('xab', '\%d18446744073709551713')" +q
# 1                                          (wrong: wrapped to 97 = 'a')
nvim --clean --headless +"echo match('xab', '\%d18446744073709551714')" +q
# 2                                          (wrong: wrapped to 98 = 'b')
nvim --clean --headless +"echo match('xab', '[\d18446744073709551713]')" +q
# 1                                          (wrong: same inside [])
```

The results are the same with either engine, e.g.
`nvim --clean --headless +"set re=1" +"echo match('xab', '\%d18446744073709551713')" +q`
(and `re=2`).

With `-DENABLE_ASAN_UBSAN=ON` (trimmed; first with `re=1`, then with `re=2`):

```
src/nvim/regexp.c:1131:8: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1844674407370955171 * 10 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t' (aka 'long')
    #0 in getdecchrs src/nvim/regexp.c:1131:8
    #1 in regatom src/nvim/regexp.c:4740:13
    #2 in regpiece src/nvim/regexp.c:5214:9
    #3 in regconcat src/nvim/regexp.c:5393:16
    #4 in regbranch src/nvim/regexp.c:5429:14
    #5 in reg src/nvim/regexp.c:5506:8
    #6 in bt_regcomp src/nvim/regexp.c:5626:7
    #7 in vim_regcomp src/nvim/regexp.c:16207:12
    #8 in find_some_match src/nvim/eval/funcs.c:3947:22

src/nvim/regexp.c:1131:8: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1844674407370955171 * 10 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t' (aka 'long')
    #0 in getdecchrs src/nvim/regexp.c:1131:8
    #1 in nfa_regatom src/nvim/regexp.c:10386:14
    #2 in nfa_regpiece src/nvim/regexp.c:10943:9
    #3 in nfa_regconcat src/nvim/regexp.c:11182:11
    #4 in nfa_regbranch src/nvim/regexp.c:11214:7
    #5 in nfa_reg src/nvim/regexp.c:11280:7
    #6 in re2post src/nvim/regexp.c:11807:7
    #7 in nfa_regcomp src/nvim/regexp.c:15960:13
    #8 in vim_regcomp src/nvim/regexp.c:16204:12
    #9 in find_some_match src/nvim/eval/funcs.c:3947:22
    #10 in f_match src/nvim/eval/funcs.c:4204:3
```


### Expected behavior


`\%d18446744073709551713` and `[\d18446744073709551713]` are treated as out of range, the same
way as `\%d99999999999`, instead of wrapping around to a small character code. No signed
integer overflow.


### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-54f94d6fc4 (master); also NVIM v0.12.0-dev (Ubuntu package 0.12.0~ubuntu1+git202601110810-d62bbe24cb)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

yes, Vim 9.2.1252 (and 9.1.2141): `\%d18446744073709551713` matches `a`. Reported as vim/vim#21668.

### Operating system/version

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic, x86_64)

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.45.0 (not terminal related, also reproduces with `--headless`)

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

build from repo (master 54f94d6, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`, `ENABLE_ASAN_UBSAN=ON`, clang); also Ubuntu system package

labels.description: This issue should be fixed in Vim first.

title: regexp: signed integer overflow in getdecchrs(), \%d18446744073709551713 matches "a"
